summary: A run that Hermes accepted and that reaches terminal before the surface projects its start makes _project_start raise ActiveTaskIdentityError, which is reported as 'acknowledgment is uncertain' and permanently latches the work-control surface UNCERTAIN.
failure_scenario: Controller receives the run's terminal event before (or immediately after) the accepted dispatch ack settles (the controller's explicit pre-ack path: _settle_dispatch pops the preack terminal and calls _settle_terminal_locked inside the ack lock, so the context has no active task when dispatch returns). _settle_start -> _project_accepted_start -> _project_start finds active_tasks empty and raises ActiveTaskIdentityError; the rollback cancel also raises ActiveTaskIdentityError and is swallowed, then _ProjectionRolledBack re-raises the original error from an except clause, so the 'except BaseException' markers are bypassed but _run_owned_operation marks health UNCERTAIN because the command was submitted via submit_start_command. User/browser then sees status 'rejected' ('Task command acknowledgment is uncertain') for work that was really accepted and finished, the terminal is still delivered, and every later start/cancel returns 'work control unavailable; restart required'. For the model tool path start_work raises to the provider. Any fast-completing or fast-failing delegation can disable task control for the rest of the session.
evidence: Synthetic stdlib reproduction (aiohttp stubbed; pytest not installed) using the real ConversationTaskController + ConversationWorkControlSurface and a fake session whose dispatch ack is released after next_update has already returned the terminal (terminal seq 5 > ack seq 1): submit_start_command -> ADMITTED, observer got one task_state rejected with the uncertain reason, surface.health == 'uncertain', a following start_work returned rejected 'work control unavailable; restart required', and next_completion still delivered status 'failed'. Passing control (same harness, terminal delivered after the ack is released): health stays 'open' and the active task_state is projected. Two existing tests assert the bad outcome as correct: tests/integration/test_natural_work_tools.py:1227-1233 (browser gets only the uncertain rejection) and :1280-1285 (asserts surface.health == 'uncertain' after a clean completion). Reachability limits: ordering needs the terminal consumed before the dispatch continuation; bridge.py writes the ack then any retained terminal back to back, and api.py emits the terminal from the SSE task, so fast runs can hit it, but end-to-end frequency was not measured and no live Hermes was used.

summary: Prior claim bridge/plugin/api terminal reason >1024 or missing reason: for assigned files, ConversationTaskController caps reason/failed summary at 1024 and api.py truncates run.failed reason to 1024 (_MAX_TERMINAL_REASON_CHARS), while the wire NonEmptyString allows 8192 and strips whitespace (my probe: protocol accepts 1100-char reason, TaskTerminalOutcome rejects it). Controller rejection then fails the generation by design; no in-repo producer reaches it, so duplicate root cause of the other-module claims, not a separate defect here. Lone-surrogate completed summaries are refused with a bounded [task-result-refusal] marker; failed-reason surrogates were not run through the controller (static only).

Prior claim 'test_completed_dispatch_idempotency_cache_is_bounded' and ack-capacity claims concern service.py/bridge.py outside this slice; not reproduced here. Within slice, ConversationWorkControlSurface binding replay is exact (same invocation_id + semantics reuses one operation, mismatched semantics latches UNCERTAIN); _admit_binding_locked can evict a done binding at 256 invocations so a replay of that evicted id would re-run, but ids are random/unique per proposal and I found no production replay of an old id, so unsupported reachability.

Cancel identity and independence: request_cancel binds to the exact run_id captured under lock, _settle_cancel requires ack session/request_event_id/scope/task_id equality and exactly one signaled run equal to that run, terminal-before-cancel-ack ordering is handled via reordered_after, and a terminal pops the cancel op. Cancel is task-scoped and independent of speech/turn cancellation (actions.cancel_foreground never calls controller). A failed session.cancel leaves a poisoned entry (task_status unavailable, retries re-raise, surface latches UNCERTAIN) without failing the controller: fail-closed accepted tradeoff, no existing authority is falsely reported.

Dispatch uncertainty: controller registers pending reservation and request sequence before any await, a session.dispatch exception fails the generation and keeps the reservation (no duplicate redispatch, no 'started' claim), accepted ack must precede active projection, a pre-ack terminal is held until the ack and rejected-ack-with-terminal faults the generation (test_terminal_before_rejected_ack_faults_generation). Terminal queue overflow (8) is not realistically reachable because the update director consumer buffers 16 mention slots first.

Router/proposals: confirmation is one-use (state cleared synchronously in _consume before any await), requires clean latched capture/readback equality or typed card, expires at 60 s, and automatic start uses a unique 'automatic_<proposal_id>' invocation id. Spoken 'Cancel task' resolves only context-active tasks, so an unacknowledged single pending start answers 'No active task to cancel' (model-tool cancel handles pending); this is a visible fail-closed refusal, not a lost authority, and is not reported. A confirmation made stale during record_user_input is consumed silently (evidence marker only): narrow window, not reported.

actions.py ConversationUpdateExecutor: reservations are released on validation, admission and spawn failure paths, claims are requeued when not delivered, close cancels foreground via host-shutdown scope separately from background tasks. When evidence admission does not return ADMITTED for a user turn, respond() proceeds without a lease; that matches the consent-missing/degraded design for other call sites (proactive path does the same), so not reported. Dependencies for pytest/mypy/ruff were not installed; analysis was static plus the stubbed stdlib reproductions above.
